entities.name: Slow CRI indication
observations: A cranial rhythmic impulse of approximately 3 cycles per minute with preserved flexion-extension amplitude is best addressed by venous sinus decompression in standard osteopathic cranial teaching.
Direct comparative evidence distinguishing venous sinus decompression from CV4, vault hold, and occipitoatlantal BLT was not retrieved; the conclusion is based on technique indications.

entities.name: Venous sinus decompression
observations: Direct gentle decompression at sutures overlying the venous sinuses is the listed technique corresponding to venous sinus drainage and normalization of a markedly slow CRI.

entities.name: CV4
observations: Compression of the fourth ventricle is generally taught to produce a still point and reduce or slow cranial rhythmic impulse, so it does not fit an already markedly slow CRI.
